##### `isReadOnly`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="isReadOnly" id="@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2.Initializer.parameter.isReadOnly"></a>

- *Type:* java.lang.Boolean|io.cdktn.cdktn.IResolvable

Whether this dashboard is read-only.

**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated and non-functional. Use `restricted_roles` instead to define which roles are required to edit the dashboard. Defaults to `false`.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/datadog/datadog/4.8.0/docs/resources/dashboard_v2#is_read_only DashboardV2#is_read_only}

- *Type:* java.util.List<java.lang.String>

The list of handles for the users to notify when changes are made to this dashboard.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/datadog/datadog/4.8.0/docs/resources/dashboard_v2#notify_list DashboardV2#notify_list}

---

##### `reflowType`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="reflowType" id="@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2.Initializer.parameter.reflowType"></a>

- *Type:* java.lang.String

The reflow type of a new dashboard layout.

Set this only when layout type is `ordered`. If set to `fixed`, the dashboard expects all widgets to have a layout, and if it's set to `auto`, widgets should not have layouts. Valid values are `auto`, `fixed`.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/datadog/datadog/4.8.0/docs/resources/dashboard_v2#reflow_type DashboardV2#reflow_type}

---

##### `restrictedRoles`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="restrictedRoles" id="@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2.Initializer.parameter.restrictedRoles"></a>

- *Type:* java.util.List<java.lang.String>

A list of role identifiers.

Only the author and users associated with at least one of these roles can edit this dashboard.

Docs at Terraform Registry: {@link https://registry.terraform.io/providers/datadog/datadog/4.8.0/docs/resources/dashboard_v2#restricted_roles DashboardV2#restricted_roles}

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2.isConstruct"></a>

```java
import io.cdktn.providers.datadog.dashboard_v2.DashboardV2;

DashboardV2.isConstruct(java.lang.Object x)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* java.lang.Object

Any object.

```java
import io.cdktn.providers.datadog.dashboard_v2.DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinition;

DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinition.builder()
    .alertId(java.lang.String)
    .vizType(java.lang.String)
//  .description(java.lang.String)
//  .hideIncompleteCostData(java.lang.Boolean|IResolvable)
//  .liveSpan(java.lang.String)
//  .time(DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinitionTime)
//  .title(java.lang.String)
//  .titleAlign(java.lang.String)
//  .titleSize(java.lang.String)
    .build();
```

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinition.property.alertId">alertId</a></code> | <code>java.lang.String</code> | The ID of the monitor used by the widget. |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinition.property.vizType">vizType</a></code> | <code>java.lang.String</code> | Whether to display the Alert Graph as a timeseries or a top list. Valid values are `timeseries`, `toplist`. |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinition.property.description">description</a></code> | <code>java.lang.String</code> | The description of the widget. |
| <code><a href="#@cdktn/provider-datadog.dashboardV2.DashboardV2WidgetAlertGraphDefinition.property.hideIncompleteCostData">hideIncompleteCostData</a></code> | <code>java.lang.Boolean\|io.cdktn.cdktn.IResolvable</code> | Hide any portion of the widget's timeframe that is incomplete due to cost data not being available. |

```java

```

- *Type:* java.lang.String

Value to apply.

Can be a single value `y = 15` or a range of values `0 < y < 10`. For Distribution widgets with `display_type` set to `percentile`, this should be a numeric percentile value (for example, `90` for P90).
